_comment: Cost prices per 1M tokens as of 2026-05-27. Hot-reloadable per Pitfall 5.
_format: { provider_model: { prompt, completion, cache_read, cache_creation_5m } } -- all values in USD per 1M tokens
_tool_fees_format: Per-call flat server-tool fees in USD (NOT per token). Plan 15-02 C1 -- published rates, facts only, never estimated.
_tool_fees_source: web_search: Anthropic published $10 per 1000 searches = $0.01/search. web_fetch: Anthropic web_fetch has no per-fetch fee (billed as input tokens only) -> 0.0 flat fee; its token cost is already in prompt_tokens. serpapi_search: SerpApi is sold as a PREPAID PLAN, so the per-search unit price is plan_monthly_price / searches_per_month -- a PUBLISHED figure, which is what makes count x unit a correct calculation and not an estimate (D-16). The authoritative value is read live from https://serpapi.com/account.json at run start and recorded with the run (output row format='serpapi_plan'), so this table carries null rather than a hardcoded tier price -- the tier itself is an open operator decision owned by plan 15.2-18. null here means 'no plan-independent published rate exists', NOT '$0.00': an unknown unit price yields cost_usd NULL + cost_pending, while a genuine Free-tier reading of $0.00 is an exact, honest zero.
_claude_opus_5_source: Quick task 260806-dn8, 2026-08-06. THE REPORT WRITER'S MODEL -- synthesis moved from google/gemini-2.5-pro to anthropic/claude-opus-5 on this date, so this row prices the three most expensive calls of every run. prompt 5.00 and completion 25.00 are the OPERATOR-SUPPLIED published rates as of 2026-08-06. cache_read and cache_creation_5m are NOT independent readings: they are Anthropic's published 0.1x and 1.25x multipliers applied to prompt, which is the IDENTICAL derivation every other anthropic/* row in this file uses (opus-4-5: 15 / 1.5 / 18.75; sonnet-4-6: 3 / 0.30 / 3.75). Recorded that way deliberately -- a derived number presented as a reading is how a cost table stops being auditable. BOTH CACHE FIELDS ARE INERT TODAY: nothing on the synthesis path sends cache_control, so neither rate can be reached by any call the engine currently makes. They exist so that a later prompt-caching change (the obvious lever -- every section call repeats the identical reports_concatenated block) prices CORRECTLY on the day it lands, instead of silently. WHY THIS ROW IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT COSMETIC: compute() returns None for an unknown model, the caller writes NULL cost_usd, and SUM(cost_usd) silently skips it -- the booked G-7 defect. Verified RED before this row was added: compute(provider='anthropic', model='claude-opus-5', ...) returned None and logged `Unknown LLM model cost ... writing NULL cost_usd`. test_synthesis_opus5.py asserts `is not None` as its own arm, with its own message, so that cannot recur.
_claude_sonnet_5_source: Quick task 260901-j6w, 2026-09-01. THE ENGINE'S WORKHORSE MODEL -- the operator moved the six production tribunal defaults (skeptic, intake, workshop, evolve, grouping, own-researcher) from claude-sonnet-4-6 to claude-sonnet-5 on this date. The skeptic stage alone measured 79% of run cost on run fb9484dd ($19.68 of $24.78 priced), so this row prices the single most expensive stage in the pipeline. prompt 2.00 and completion 10.00 are the OFFICIAL published Anthropic rates (pricing page, verified 2026-09-01), as are cache_read 0.20 and cache_creation_5m 2.50 -- and note that those two ALSO happen to equal Anthropic's standard 0.1x and 1.25x multipliers applied to prompt, the identical derivation every other anthropic/* row in this file uses (opus-4-5: 15 / 1.5 / 18.75; opus-5: 5 / 0.50 / 6.25; sonnet-4-6: 3 / 0.30 / 3.75). They agree, so nothing is being passed off as a reading that is not one. WHY THIS ROW IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT COSMETIC: compute() returns None for an unknown model, the caller writes NULL cost_usd, and SUM(cost_usd) silently skips it -- the booked G-7 defect. Swapping the model without adding this row would have destroyed cost tracking for 79% of every run's spend, silently. The sonnet-4-6 row below is DELIBERATELY RETAINED: historical runs, the untouched critique/ tooling, and the legacy claude deep-research adapter (tools/claude_adapter.py) all still resolve against it. THE PROJECTED SAVING IS ARITHMETIC, NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT: 33% cheaper per token on paper, ~13% after adjusting for the ~30% token inflation of the newer tokenizer, but a different model may use different token volumes AND a different number of tool-use turns. The real figure is unknown until a run executes.
_gemini_2_5_pro_tiering: Quick task 260901-lf2, 2026-09-01. cache_read CORRECTED 0.3125 -> 0.125 against Google published pricing (verified 2026-09-01). The old 0.3125 was NOT a reading: it was prompt x 0.25, the Anthropic-style derivation this file uses elsewhere, applied to a vendor that does not price that way. prompt 1.25 and completion 10.0 ARE correct and are deliberately left alone. ⚠ TIERED PRICING, AND THIS TABLE ENCODES ONLY THE LOWER TIER: $1.25/$10 applies to prompts <=200k tokens; ABOVE 200k the rates are $2.50/$15. `_rate()` returns ONE FLAT NUMBER per field and has no notion of a tier -- the identical limitation already recorded for openai/gpt-5.6-sol at `_gpt_5_6_sol_long_context`. So a gemini-2.5-pro call with more than 200k prompt tokens is UNDER-REPORTED by 2x/1.5x here, and a run total containing one is a FLOOR, not a settled figure. Recorded rather than fixed, for the same reason given there: making compute()/_rate() tier-aware is a risky change to a 7-year-retention audit path and is not being smuggled into a model-swap task.
_gemini_2_5_flash_correction: Quick task 260901-lf2, 2026-09-01. THREE FIELDS CORRECTED against Google published pricing (verified 2026-09-01) -- the previous row was STALE AND UNDERSTATED REAL SPEND: prompt 0.15 -> 0.30, completion 0.60 -> 2.50 (a 4.2x correction -- Google raised Flash output pricing sharply and this table never followed), cache_read 0.0375 -> 0.03. THIS IS A CORRECTION, NOT A PRICE CHANGE: the money was always being spent at these rates; the table was reporting less than the invoice. Every historical run total computed from the old row therefore UNDER-STATES its Flash cost, and cost_usd is stored per-row at write time, so those historical rows are NOT retroactively repaired by this edit. THE ROW IS DELIBERATELY RETAINED even though five of the six Flash sites moved to gemini-3.7-flash on this date: the synthesis CLAIM DISTILLER (pipeline/synthesis/steps.py `_DISTILLER_MODEL`) still calls this model, and historical audit rows reference the key. Deleting it would take the compute() unknown-model branch and write NULL cost_usd -- the booked G-7 defect.
_gemini_3_7_flash_source: Quick task 260901-lf2, 2026-09-01. THE TRIBUNAL WORKHORSE JUDGE -- the operator moved FIVE Flash sites to this model on this date (gates, grouping, report_planner, workshop_rank, workshop_admission; workshop_evolve._META_MODEL follows workshop_rank by inheritance). Rates are Google published pricing, verified 2026-09-01. ⚠⚠ THESE ARE INTRODUCTORY RATES, VALID THROUGH 2026-12-31. ON 2027-01-01 THEY DOUBLE to prompt 1.50 / completion 7.50 / cache_read 0.15 per Google published pricing. A silent doubling in January would otherwise read as a cost regression from nowhere, with no code change to explain it and nothing in this file to point at -- so it is written down BEFORE it happens. WHEN THAT DATE PASSES, UPDATE THE THREE NUMBERS AND THIS NOTE TOGETHER. WHY THIS ROW IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT COSMETIC: compute() returns None for an unknown model, the caller writes NULL cost_usd, and SUM(cost_usd) silently skips it -- the booked G-7 defect. Swapping five call sites without adding this row would have written NULL costs for every gate, grouping, planner and tournament call in every run, silently. THE COST INCREASE IS ACCEPTED AND MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED AWAY: 3.7 THINKS DESPITE thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget=0, so output tokens rose 4.2x across the 267-prompt replay of run fb9484dd. Projected on that real run, Flash cost goes $0.54 -> $2.04, about +$1.50/run. That projection is arithmetic over replayed token counts, NOT an observed run total -- NO RUN HAS YET EXECUTED ON 3.7.
_comment_deep_research_preview: Plan 15-02 C1: the per-TOKEN rates below are the published Gemini 2.5 Pro base rates (the underlying deep-research model) -- these are FACTS, applied only when usageMetadata is present. Google does NOT publish an itemized grounding/search tool fee for these preview deep-research agents, so that un-itemizable fee is NEVER estimated: the caller sets run.cost_pending=True and the exact amount is backfilled from GCP billing. No displayed number is a guess.
_gpt_5_6_sol_source: Plan 15.8-08, operator ruling `published-rates`, 2026-08-04. THESE ARE THIRD-PARTY FIGURES, NOT A PRIMARY SOURCE, and that qualification is part of the record. OpenAI's own pricing page (openai.com/api/pricing) returned HTTP 403 and could not be read. The four numbers below come from four aggregator pages that agree with each other -- benchlm.ai/openai/api-pricing and openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-5.6-sol (both fetched directly), plus aipricing.guru/openai-pricing and modelpricing.ai/models/openai -- all retrieved 2026-08-04. AGGREGATORS COPY EACH OTHER, SO THEIR AGREEMENT IS NOT INDEPENDENCE: four sources concurring is weaker evidence than it looks, and it is recorded that way deliberately. The operator accepted them on exactly that basis rather than on a primary reading. CONFLICT ON THE RECORD: gpt-5.6-sol launched 2026-07-09; the Terra and Luna variants were price-cut on 2026-07-30 while Sol stayed at its launch rate. One aggregator claimed Sol's input rate also fell to $2.50 and is contradicted by the other three. $5.00 was taken. If a primary reading ever becomes available, re-verify prompt first -- that is the field the sources disagreed on.
_gpt_5_6_sol_anomalies: THREE WAYS THIS ENTRY BREAKS THE PATTERN OF EVERY OTHER openai/* ROW IN THIS FILE. Read before 'correcting' any of them. (1) cache_creation_5m: 6.25 is the FIRST NON-ZERO cache-write value for any openai model here -- every other openai entry is 0.0. GPT-5.6 changed OpenAI's caching economics; cache writes bill at 1.25x uncached input. It is not a copy-paste from the Anthropic block. NOTE THE LABEL IS IMPORTED: the field name carries Anthropic's 5-MINUTE-TTL naming, while OpenAI documents a 30-MINUTE minimum TTL for this model. The NUMBER is right for this model; the FIELD NAME is a schema artefact shared with Anthropic and does not describe OpenAI's TTL. (2) cache_read: 0.50 is a 90% discount off prompt, where gpt-4o is 50% off and o3 / o4-mini are 75% off. This is NOT a typo -- do not 'fix' it to 2.50. (3) completion: 30.00 is 6x prompt, a wider spread than gpt-4o's 4x.
_gpt_5_6_sol_long_context: A KNOWN, DELIBERATE IMPRECISION -- OPERATOR RULED 2026-08-04: RECORD IT, DO NOT FIX IT. gpt-5.6-sol has a LONG-CONTEXT METER: above 272,000 INPUT tokens, the ENTIRE request re-bills at 2x input and 1.5x output (prompt $10.00, completion $45.00, cache_read $1.00). `_rate()` in cost_table.py returns ONE FLAT NUMBER per field and has no notion of a tier, so the rates in this entry are EXACTLY CORRECT BELOW 272K AND UNDER-REPORT BY 2x/1.5x ABOVE IT. Making compute()/_rate() tier-aware was considered and DECLINED: it is too risky a change to the audit cost path one plan before deploy, in code that feeds a 7-year-retention record. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT MUST NEVER BE PRESENTED AS A TOTAL: this is the THIRD mechanically distinct reason a run total is a FLOOR rather than a settled figure. The other two are (a) the gpt-5.6-sol rows that wrote NULL cost_usd before this ruling, which SUM(cost_usd) silently skipped, and (b) WR-02 -- a failed or timed-out angle emits NO assignment_yield row at all, so SUM misses it with no column to explain the gap. OBLIGATION HANDED TO PLAN 15.8-15: measure the ACTUAL prompt_tokens on the five openai deep-research calls against the 272K boundary and report whether it bound. If it did, this entry is corrected with real measured data -- it is not to be guessed now.

serpapi/google._note: Phase 15.2 plan 12 (D-16). SerpApi is a SEARCH provider, not an LLM: it has no token pricing at all, so all four per-token rates are a true 0.0. This entry exists purely so compute() resolves the 'serpapi/google' key instead of taking the unknown-model NULL branch -- the ENTIRE cost of a SerpApi audit row is the per-search fee, passed in as serpapi_search_count x serpapi_unit_price_usd. Do not add a unit price here; it is per-run, not per-table, because the plan can change.
